subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should OpenClaw support explicit provider/model overrides for main-session `systemEvent` cron jobs, and if so should the public contract be `payload.model`, top-level cron fields, or a `sessionOverride` block?
rationale: Current code treats system events as text-only main-session injections; adding model overrides crosses provider routing, cron persistence, session-state, UI/CLI, and heartbeat semantics that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design an explicit override contract
options.body: Add a public cron-owned provider/model override shape, validate it like isolated cron payload models, and prove both wake modes do not leak or corrupt session state.

options.title: Keep system events text-only
options.body: Document this path as unsupported and steer cheap scheduled model calls to isolated/current/custom-session `agentTurn` jobs.

options.title: Defer into broader cron schema work
options.body: Track this with the broader cron schema and cost-control API work so model, context, timeout, and spend semantics are decided together.

recommendation.title: Design an explicit override contract
recommendation.body: Add a public cron-owned provider/model override shape, validate it like isolated cron payload models, and prove both wake modes do not leak or corrupt session state.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current mix of cron runtime/schema history and product-sensitive scope decisions for the related UI work.
